faq.title: What works with what
faq.lead: The short version: services you connect do everything, services you paste a link from are import sources. The table below spells it out service by service.

matrix.question: What exactly can each service do?
matrix.caption: What each music service supports in Synqit

connect.question: Which services can I connect to Synqit?
connect.answer: The ones marked Connect in the table above. You sign in once, and from then on Synqit reads and writes playlists in your own library, so the features that service supports are open to you: event playlists, shared playlists, and transfers.

link.question: Can I use a service I cannot connect?
link.answer: Yes, as a source. Paste the link to a public playlist and Synqit rebuilds it in the service you connected. There is no account to link and no password to give. Synqit never writes anything back to the source, and private playlists cannot be read.

guests.question: Do my guests need an account to add songs?
guests.answer: No. They open your link, search, and add. No app to install, no sign-up, whatever service they listen on. The playlist itself lives in your own library, on the service you host from.

syncDirection.question: Does a shared playlist sync both ways?
syncDirection.answer: No. Followers receive every track you add, on whichever connected service they use. Anything they add on their side stays theirs, so your playlist is never changed by someone else.

skipped.question: Why do some tracks get skipped?
skipped.answer: Catalogues differ between services, and a song that exists on one is not always on another. Where a source carries a recording ID, as Deezer does, matches are exact. Where it only gives a title as free text, as YouTube does, a few tracks can match a different version or be missed.

linkPrivacy.question: Who can open my playlist link?
linkPrivacy.answer: Anyone you send it to, which is what makes it easy for guests. You stay in control: remove any track, close the playlist when the party is over, and revoke or regenerate the link at any time.

leaving.question: What happens to my playlists if I stop using Synqit?
leaving.answer: Nothing. Every playlist Synqit creates is a real playlist in your own library, on your own account. It stays there, with all its tracks, whether or not you keep using Synqit.
